label: Clear_Cell_RCC
answer_markdown:
## Key Facts
- Most common type of renal cell carcinoma in adults.
- Characterized by clear cytoplasm and delicate chicken-wire vasculature.
- Frequently associated with loss of chromosome 3p and VHL gene mutation.
- High-grade tumors exhibit aggressive behavior with metastasis potential.
- Typically negative or focal for CK7; positive for CA9/CAIX.

## Terminology
- **Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma (CCRCC)**
- Synonyms: Conventional renal cell carcinoma.

## Essential and Desirable Diagnostic Criteria
- **Essential:**
  - Clear cytoplasm with distinct cell borders.
  - Delicate chicken-wire vasculature.
  - Defining molecular alterations (loss of chromosome 3p, VHL mutations).
  - Immunohistochemistry: positive for CA9/CAIX with box-like membranous staining, typically negative or focal for CK7.
- **Desirable:**
  - Nests or alveolar growth pattern.
  - Evidence of necrosis or hemorrhage in high-grade cases.

## Etiology/Pathogenesis
- Associated with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease.
- Chromosome 3p deletion and VHL mutations drive pathogenesis.

## Clinical Issues
- **Epidemiology:** Most common in adults.
- **Site:** Primarily arises in the kidney.
- **Presentation:** May present as a mass, often detected incidentally.
- **Prognosis:** Variable, high-grade tumors have worse outcomes.

## Macroscopic
- Yellow-orange cut surface, typically well-circumscribed.
- Potential areas of necrosis and hemorrhage depending on grade.

## Microscopic
- Clear cytoplasm, distinct cell borders.
- **Patterns:**
  - Nests and sheets of cells.
  - Delicate chicken-wire capillary network.

## Ancillary Tests
- **Immunohistochemistry:**
  - CA9/CAIX: positive, box-like membranous pattern.
  - CK7: negative or focal.
- **Molecular/Genetics:**
  - VHL gene mutations.
  - Loss of chromosome 3p.

## Differential Diagnosis
| Feature                     | Clear Cell RCC      | Papillary RCC     | Chromophobe RCC     | Clear Cell Papillary RCC |
|-----------------------------|---------------------|-------------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| Cytoplasm                   | Clear               | Foamy             | Clear to pale       | Clear                    |
| Vascularity                 | Chicken-wire        | Fibrovascular     | None                | None                     |
| CK7                         | Negative/focal      | Positive          | Positive            | Positive                 |
| CA9/CAIX                    | Positive (strong)   | Negative          | Negative            | Positive                 |

- **Papillary RCC:** Foamy histiocytes; positive for CK7.
- **Chromophobe RCC:** Pale cytoplasm; raisinoid nuclei; positive for CK7.
- **Clear Cell Papillary RCC:** Clear cytoplasm with low nuclear grade; positive for CK7 and CA9.

![Clear cell renal tumors](https://www.pathologyoutlines.com/imgau/kidneytumormalignantrccShah01.jpg)

cards.excerpt: Entity: Collecting duct carcinoma Section: microscopic CDC typically shows tubular and tubulopapillary architectural patterns with irregular, infiltrating glands and associated desmoplastic stroma. Solid nested or sheet-like, trabecular, cord-like individual cells, as well as microcystic patterns, may also be present; a subset show an infiltrative nodular papillary component. The tumour edge is poorly defined, with tumour cells infiltrating between tubules and glomeruli of the adjacent renal parenchyma, which may show dysplasia or atypia within uninvolved tubules. There is often a prominent inflammatory reaction including a neutrophil infiltrate within and around the tumour. Lymphovascular invasion and regional lymph node involvement are common at nephrectomy. The cells exhibit high-grade nuclear features, usually with eosinophilic cytoplasm, but they can be clear or amphophilic. Cells lining tubules are often cuboidal, although columnar and hobnail cells are common. Nuclei are large, vesicular, and highly pleomorphic, with prominent nucleoli. cards.title: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney
cards.entity_name: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney
cards.excerpt: Entity: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney definition: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney (CCSK) is a rare malignant renal tumour of childhood characterized histologically by variably clear tumour cells and distinctive arborizing fibrovascular septa, and molecularly by BCOR mutations or YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion. related_terminology: Not recommended: bone-metastasizing renal tumour of childhood. essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: characteristic histomorphology of ovoid tumour cells with nuclear and/or cytoplasmic clearing at least focally, distinctive arborizing fibrovascular septa, and immunoreactivity for cyclin D1 and BCOR. Desirable: features for cases with atypical histomorphology or immunophenotype include molecular identification of BCOR exon 15 ITD or of YWHAE::NUTM2 or BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion.

cards.title: Clear cell adenocarcinoma
cards.excerpt: Entity: Clear cell adenocarcinoma definition: Clear cell adenocarcinoma is a malignant epithelial tumour consisting of Müllerian-type epithelium with clear cell morphology. related_terminology: None essential_and_desirable_diagnostic_criteria: Essential: a tumour with clear and hobnail cells in a solid, tubulocystic, confluent, or complex papillary pattern; exclusion of metastasis. Desirable: immunoreactivity for CK7 and PAX8; negativity for mesothelial markers and RCCm.

cards.title: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour
cards.entity_name: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour
cards.excerpt: Entity: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour Section: clinical The vast majority of these tumours are incidentally detected. --- The tumour accounts for approximately 3% of cases of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in adults, with an age range of 8–88 years. The tumours can occur in end-stage renal disease. Tumours of identical morphology that occur in patients with von Hippel–Lindau syndrome appear genomically related to clear cell RCC and distinct from CCPRCT. In 20% and 25% of cases, patients have multifocal and bilateral renal tumours, respectively, and in > 50% of these patients, there is a discordant subtype.

cards.title: Rhabdoid tumour of the kidney
cards.excerpt: Entity: Rhabdoid tumour of the kidney Section: ancillary_studies For rhabdoid tumour of the kidney with SMARCA4 inactivation, SMARCA4 (BRG1) immunohistochemistry may be used; this shows a loss of nuclear staining in tumour cells and normal expression in all other cells. Other than by loss of SMARCB1 (INI1) immunostaining, rhabdoid tumour of the kidney and indeed all rhabdoid tumours have a diverse pattern of immunoreactivity, including multiple keratins and vimentin, but also SMA, synaptophysin, and GFAP. Nonspecific polyphenotypic patterns for other antibodies may occur due to trapping of antibodies in hyaline inclusions such as EMA and pancytokeratin. Importantly, over half of rhabdoid tumours show CD99 expression, which may add to the morphological confusion with Ewing sarcoma. Although differential diagnoses are limited in cases with typical morphology and immunohistochemistry, cellular mesoblastic nephroma, plump cell pattern, and clear cell sarcoma of the kidney may be considered. Several renal cell carcinoma morphologies, including clear cell renal cell carcinoma and renal medullary carcinoma, may show rhabdoid morphology with or without SMARCB1 (INI) loss.

cards.excerpt: Entity: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney Section: diagnostic_molecular_pathology Three characteristic mutations of CCSK are (in decreasing order of frequency) BCOR exon 15 ITD, YWHAE::NUTM2 gene fusion, and BCOR::CCNB3 gene fusion. These three mutations are mutually exclusive.

cards.title: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour
cards.entity_name: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour
cards.excerpt: Entity: Clear cell papillary renal cell tumour Section: diagnostic_molecular_pathology There are specific molecular pathological features diagnostic of this tumour. Importantly, this tumour lacks chromosome 3p loss and alterations of VHL characteristic of clear cell RCC, and no mutations in TSC1, TSC2, MTOR, or ELOC (TCBE1) (all characteristic of RCC with fibromyomatous or leiomyomatous stroma) have been reported.

cards.title: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumour of the kidney
cards.entity_name: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumour of the kidney
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumour of the kidney Section: ancillary_studies The stromal component is typically positive for actin, desmin, CD10, ER, and PR and frequently the luteinized stromal cells express inhibin and calretinin. Cathepsin K is negative. The epithelial component is PAX2/8-positive. Immunohistochemistry is helpful in the exclusion of renal synovial sarcoma, clear cell papillary tumour, and tubulocystic renal cell carcinoma.

cards.entity_name: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumour of the kidney
cards.excerpt: Entity: Mixed epithelial and stromal tumour of the kidney Section: cytology Cytological diagnosis may be difficult because aspiration specimens may contain occasional groups of cohesive renal epithelial cells, raising the differential diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma.

cards.title: PEComa
cards.excerpt: Entity: PEComa Section: differential_diagnosis In childhood, the diagnosis of PEComa may be extremely challenging because of a relatively large differential diagnosis, which differs depending on the tumour site and can include clear cell sarcoma of soft tissue (also known as melanoma of soft parts), alveolar soft part sarcoma, smooth muscle tumours, MiT-family translocation renal cell carcinoma, clear cell sarcoma of the kidney, gastrointestinal stromal tumour, and metastatic melanoma.

No definite specific etiology but common in end stage kidney disease (ESRD)
Could arise from progenitor-like cell population in proximal renal tubules in ESRD (Am J Pathol 2011;178:828, Am J Pathol 2019;189:2046)

cards.title: Papillary — Treatment
cards.excerpt:
Resection or ablation for localized disease
Selective MET kinase inhibitor, MET / VEGF inhibitor, multitargeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and PD-1 / PDL1 inhibitors for advanced or metastatic disease (Curr Opin Urol 2022;32:344)
For advanced metastatic PRCC cabozantinib shows higher efficacy over sunitinib and other MET kinase inhibitors (Lancet 2021;397:695)

cards.title: Chromophobe — Epidemiology
cards.excerpt:
Third most common renal cell carcinoma (RCC), accounting for 5 - 7% of cases (Asian J Urol 2022;9:1)
In the United States, ~ 3,200 new cases were recorded in 2020 (CA Cancer J Clin 2020;70:7)
Slight M > F; median age of 59 years (range: 17 - 92) (Virchows Arch 2020;476:409)
Compared to clear cell RCC, ChRCC is more frequently diagnosed in younger females (Clin Genitourin Cancer 2019;17:373)

Clear cell RCC represents ~65 - 70% of adult renal carcinomas
Second and third most common RCC subtypes are papillary (10 - 15%) and chromophobe RCC (5%)

cards.title: Renal cell carcinoma overview — Epidemiology
cards.heading: Epidemiology
cards.text_excerpt:
Incidence: worldwide as of 2020, it is the seventh most common cancer in men (271,249 new cases) and the tenth most common in women (160,039 new cases)
M:F = ~2:1; some subtypes are more common in women (e.g., eosinophilic solid and cystic RCC)
Patients are usually > 50 years old; peak incidence between the ages of 60 and 70 years
~70% of new cases occur in countries with high socioeconomic development
Estimated lifetime prevalence of 2.3% for men and 1.3% for women in the U.S. (JAMA 2024;332:1001)
RCC incidence varies widely from region to region with the highest rates (as of 2018) in Belarus (16.8 cases per 100.000 population), followed by other Central and Eastern European countries
High incidence rates of RCC are also found in the U.S., with an estimated ~81,800 new cases in 2023 and over 14,000 deaths from RCC each year (CA Cancer J Clin 2017;67:7, JAMA 2024;332:1001)

cards.title: Renal cell carcinoma overview — Hereditary renal cell tumors
cards.heading: Hereditary renal cell tumors
cards.text_excerpt:
Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome
Autosomal dominant, due to germline mutation of VHL tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 3p25
Associated renal lesions: clear cell renal cell carcinoma, benign or atypical renal cysts and numerous microscopic nodules of clear cells (Semin Diagn Pathol 2024;41:20)
RCC in VHL syndrome can be multifocal or bilateral in 50% (eMedicine: Von Hippel-Lindau Syndrome Imaging [Accessed 7 November 2024])
Clear cell RCC in VHL syndrome may show branching tubulopapillary growth and apical polarization of nuclei resembling clear cell papillary renal cell tumor but shows characteristic molecular and immunohistochemical profile of clear cell RCC
Other associated lesions: hemangioblastomas of cerebellum and retina, pancreatic or liver cysts, clear cell tumors of other sites, papillary cystadenoma of epididymis, pheochromocytoma

cards.title: Renal cell carcinoma overview — Usually multiple cutaneous or uterine leiomyomas at a younger age
cards.heading: Usually multiple cutaneous or uterine leiomyomas at a younger age
cards.text_excerpt:
Associated renal tumors are classified as a separate entity in the current WHO 2022, termed FH deficient RCC, with distinctive morphology showing a combination of architectural patterns with at least focal papillary growth and large nuclei with a very prominent, inclusion-like eosinophilic nucleoli surrounded by perinucleolar haloes
Rare, reported cases of testicular Leydig cell tumors (Med Rep 2024;5:100057)
Genetic testing is always warranted for these aggressive tumors, as purely somatic biallelic FH mutations may occur (rarely in the setting of FH deficient RCC but commonly in older patients with solitary FH deficient uterine leiomyomas)

cards.title: Renal cell carcinoma overview — BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome
cards.heading: BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome
cards.text_excerpt:
Autosomal dominant, due to heterozygous germline mutations in BAP1 tumor suppressor gene encoding BRCA associated protein 1
Associated with uveal and cutaneous melanocytic tumors / atypical Spitz tumors, cutaneous melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, malignant mesotheliomas, meningiomas and other tumors
Renal lesions: usually clear cell RCC with aggressive phenotype; isolated reports of non-clear cell tumors; may be multifocal (JAMA Netw Open 2021;4:e2132615)
